expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = | { status: 'trialing'; trialEndDate: Date } | ... — tagged on `status`

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each arm lists only its own fields; "You literally cannot construct a subscription with both `trialEndDate` and `cancelReason`"

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: No assertNever, no switch with a `never` default; only an `if (sub.status === 'past_due')` narrowing example

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: No ID fields or branded types at all; `cancelReason: string` is a bare string

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function or state-change constraint is mentioned

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "you can't access `cancelReason` on an active subscription" and "cannot construct a subscription with both `trialEndDate` and `cancelReason` — the compiler rejects it"

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is the discriminated union; no optional-field interface offered
